elements.content: Grammar focus: End-Weight Principle & Heavy-NP Shift.

Core Rule: Postpose complex, heavily modified noun phrases to the end of the sentence ( Heavy-NP Shift ), especially after short verbs or prepositional phrases.

Standard (Top-Heavy) — Heavy Object + Short Verb: A multi-billion dollar fund aimed at green transition was established . (Awkward)
Heavy-NP Shifted — Introductory Verb/It + Heavy Object: The council established a multi-billion dollar fund aimed at green transition. (Balanced)
Extraposed Shift — It + Verb + Heavy Clause: It was made clear to all delegates that compliance is non-negotiable.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence correctly applies Heavy-NP Shift for structural balance?
options: The minister explained to the assembly the complex economic mechanisms underlying the crisis.
The minister the complex economic mechanisms underlying the crisis explained to the assembly.

elements.content: 2. Why apply Heavy-NP Shift in complex technical writing?
options: To avoid awkward top-heavy sentences and ensure smooth information processing

Second grammar point of the lesson: Extraposition of Clausal Subjects. Core Rule: Move heavy clausal subjects to the end of the sentence and insert dummy It in subject position: It + Passive / Adjectival Predicate + That-Clause / Infinitive Clause .
